# Ensure every Main Street card has dedicated card art (1024×1024 source)

## Problem statement

Every Main Street card renders a square art zone in its top-left corner, but
**108 of the 171 unique cards in `card-data.csv` currently render the same
generic `Fallback` sprite**, so the bulk of the deck is visually
indistinguishable. A player cannot tell an `Upgrade to Patisserie` from a
`Chef` from a `Rainy Day` at a glance, which undermines the 64×64 left-art
redesign's whole purpose.

## Users

- **Player (market / hand / street):** needs to recognise a card by its art
  without reading the title — especially when cards overlap in hand or stack
  on the street.
- **Content author:** needs a documented, testable rule for what art a card
  resolves to, so new cards cannot silently reintroduce `Fallback` art.
- **Engine maintainer:** needs one art-resolution path shared by the runtime
  generator and the static SVG exporter, guarded by a regression test.

User stories:

- As a player, when I look at the market, I can tell any two cards apart by
  their art alone.
- As an upgrade card, I show the art of the business I enhance under my new
  display name, so my purpose is obvious.
- As a content author, when I add a card to `card-data.csv`, the test suite
  tells me if I forgot to give it art.

## Producer decisions (answered 2026-09-26)

| # | Question | Decision |
|---|----------|----------|
| Q1 | Art scope / strategy | **Option A — reuse-first.** Actively **duplicate the existing art under the new (card/display) name**, and produce **new art only where necessary** (no suitable existing art). |
| Q2 | Art production ownership | **The producer will produce the new sprites.** This item still owns the mapping, resolver, regeneration tooling and the drift guard. |
| Q3 | Event mapping granularity | **Map events by `trigger` × `targetSynergy` category** (a documented, generated mapping). |

## Producer decisions (answered 2026-09-29)

| # | Question | Decision |
|---|----------|----------|
| Q4 | Source-art size | The producer provides **1024×1024** source art (`<Name>_1024_x_1024.png`). The “64×64” is the on-card display zone, not the production size. |
| Q5 | Staff art granularity | **One sprite per staff role** (24 sprites). |
| Q6 | Event-category art | **Unique (bespoke) sprite per `(trigger, targetSynergy)` category** — representatives are not reused. |
| Q7 | Drift-guard tightening | **Yes** — tighten the guard to a strict “zero `Fallback` for every card in `card-data.csv`” assertion once the sprites land, in the same change. |
| Q8 | Duplicate-name clash | **Rename to remove the clashes**: business `Florist` → `Flower Shop`; event `Community Garden` → `Garden Party`. |

Art-production ownership (Q2, 2026-09-26) is unchanged: the producer supplies
all new source sprites.

## Existing state (verified 2026-09-26, `dev` @ 933644bc)

Resolution path (all four card families call it with the card's `name`):

- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetCardArt.ts` → `resolveCardArtName()` /
  `hasDedicatedCardArt()`: (1) spelling alias → (2) exact name → (3)
  `Fallback`.
- Map built by `example-games/main-street/scripts/generate-main-street-card-art.mjs`
  from committed `sprites/<Name>_1024_x_1024.png` files into
  `example-games/main-street/card-art-map.json`.
- A second consumer, `example-games/main-street/scripts/generate-main-street-card-svgs.mjs`,
  duplicates the alias/lookup logic and must be kept in step.

Verified counts:

- `card-data.csv`: **173 rows / 171 unique names** (duplicate names across
  families: `Florist` = business + staff, `Community Garden` = community-space
  + event → name-keyed resolution shares one sprite).
- Committed sprites: **62 dedicated + `Fallback`** (63 map entries).
- Cards resolving today: **65** (63 exact + 2 via aliases).
- **Cards rendering `Fallback`: 108**:

| Family              | Cards | Resolving | Missing |
|---------------------|------:|----------:|--------:|
| business            |    30 |        28 |       2 |
| community-space     |     8 |         1 |       7 |
| upgrade             |    39 |         0 |      39 |
| staff               |    25 |         1 |      24 |
| event               |    71 |        35 |      36 |
| **Total**           |  **173** | **65** | **108** |

Every missing card already has an `art_notes` description in `card-data.csv`
(the source the existing 1024×1024 sprites were built from). There is **no
in-repo image generator** — the existing sprites were committed out-of-band
(commit `05026750`), and the producer will continue producing new art the same
way.

## Size clarification (reviewed 2026-09-29)

The “64×64” in the original title is the **on-card display zone** — a layout
dimension in SVG user units — **not** the size of the source art to produce.
Code review of the generator and renderer confirms three distinct layers:

| Layer | Size | Where | Role |
|-------|-----:|-------|------|
| On-card art zone | 64×64 | `src/scenes/MainStreetCardSvgGenerator.ts` (`GRAPHIC_*`) | SVG layout box only |
| Embedded bitmap | 256×256 | `src/card-art-map.json` (`artResolution`) | WebP `data:` URI in the SVG |
| **Source art** | **1024×1024** | `src/sprites/<Name>_1024_x_1024.png` | Generator input |

`src/scripts/generate-main-street-card-art.mjs` only loads files named
`<Name>_1024_x_1024.png` (`SOURCE_SUFFIX = '_1024_x_1024.png'`) and downscales
each to 256×256 WebP (`ART_RESOLUTION = 256`). Phaser rasterises the card SVG
at `qualityScale = max(4, dpr)`, so the 64×64 zone needs a ≥256×256 bitmap to
stay crisp; a 64×64 source would be stretched ~4× and appear pixelated.

**Produce every new sprite at 1024×1024**, named `<Name>_1024_x_1024.png`, in
`src/sprites/`. The legacy `<Name>_64_x_64.png` files are superseded
thumbnails and are not read by the generator.

## Progress (2026-09-29)

The mapping/resolver/tooling + pending-aware drift guard landed on `dev` as
commit `4b80741` (full unit suite green): `src/card-art-map.json` is now
`version: 3`. Real coverage rose from **65 → 95 of 171** unique cards.

**Duplicate names split (commit `874f419`).** On producer decision Q8 the two
duplicate card names were renamed, so all **173 card names are now unique**:

- business `Florist` → **`Flower Shop`** — keeps the existing rose sprite
  (renamed `Flower Shop_1024_x_1024.png`); its `upgradePath` and
  `Upgrade to Garden Center`'s `targetBusiness` both follow.
- event `Community Garden` → **`Garden Party`** — now needs its own art and maps
  to the `Investment__` category until then.
- staff `Florist` keeps its name; its business restriction is now
  `Flower Shop|Commerce|Culture`.

Card IDs are intentionally unchanged (`biz-florist`, `evt-community-garden`) to
preserve save/challenge compatibility. After the split, **95 of 173** cards
resolve and **78** still render `Fallback`: the staff `Florist` and event
`Garden Party` joined the pending set, giving **46 distinct source sprites** to
produce.

## Desired change (confirmed strategy)

1. **Upgrades (39) — duplicate target art under the new display name.**
   For each `Upgrade to …`, copy the art of its `targetBusiness` to a new
   source sprite named after the upgrade's `newDisplayName` (all 39 are
   distinct, no collisions, and none is already a sprite). Seven targets are
   themselves gaps, so their art must be produced first: `Cafe`,
   `Health Kiosk`, `Laundromat`, `Library`, `Park`, `Playground`,
   `Town Fountain`.
2. **Business / community-space gaps (9) — new art.** `Laundromat`, `Cafe` and
   all community spaces except `Community Garden`: `Park`, `Library`,
   `Playground`, `Town Fountain`, `Health Kiosk`, `Community Shelter`,
   `Public Art`.
3. **Staff (25) — new staff art.** **One sprite per staff role** (confirmed
   2026-09-29), produced by the producer. The split moved `Florist` (staff)
   off the shared business sprite, so all 25 roles need art.
4. **Events (37) — category mapping.** Map each event to a category sprite
   keyed by `(trigger, targetSynergy)`; **unique (bespoke) art per category**
   (confirmed 2026-09-29), produced by the producer. `Garden Party` joined the
   category-mapped set after the split.
5. **Resolver / map.** Extend the generated mapping (and/or `CARD_ART_ALIASES`)
   so both consumers agree and regeneration stays deterministic; keep
   `Fallback` only as the genuine last resort.
6. **Drift guard.** Add a unit test over `card-data.csv` asserting full
   coverage and failing when a new art-less card appears.

## Required art (derived)

| Group | Cards | Mechanism | New sprites |
|-------|------:|-----------|------------:|
| Upgrade | 39 | Duplicate `targetBusiness` art under each upgrade's `newDisplayName` | 0 new (39 copies) |
| Business + community-space gaps | 9 | New source art | 9 |
| Staff | 25 | New source art — one per role | 25 |
| Event | 37 | Unique `(trigger × targetSynergy)` category art — 12 categories | 12 |
| **Total distinct source sprites** | | | **46** |

Event categories for the 36 missing events (representative = an event with
dedicated art today in the same category, available to duplicate):

| `trigger` | `targetSynergy` | Cards | Existing representative |
|-----------|-----------------|------:|-------------------------|
| Incident  | (none)          | 9 | Tax Audit |
| Incident  | Culture         | 1 | Cultural Grant |
| Incident  | Entertainment   | 1 | Noise Complaint |
| Incident  | Food            | 6 | *(none — new)* |
| Incident  | Health          | 1 | *(none — new)* |
| Incident  | Service         | 4 | *(none — new)* |
| Investment| (none)          | 3 | Charity Drive |
| Investment| Commerce        | 1 | Grand Opening Sale |
| Investment| Entertainment   | 3 | Street Performer |
| Investment| Food            | 2 | Harvest Festival |
| Investment| Health          | 3 | *(none — new)* |
| Investment| Service         | 2 | *(none — new)* |

Existing dedicated event art (35 events) is retained; only the 36 missing
events are category-mapped. **The producer confirmed on 2026-09-29 that each of
the 12 categories gets unique (bespoke) art** — the “existing representative”
column above is informational only and is not reused.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Every **unique** card name in `card-data.csv` resolves via
   `MainStreetCardArt.hasDedicatedCardArt()` to a **non-`Fallback`** sprite
   (documented alias/category mapping counts); currently 65/171.
2. All 39 upgrade cards resolve to art duplicated from their `targetBusiness`
   under the upgrade's `newDisplayName`; no upgrade renders `Fallback`.
3. All 24 staff cards resolve to dedicated staff art; no staff card renders
   `Fallback`.
4. All 36 missing event cards resolve to a documented
   `(trigger, targetSynergy)` category sprite; no event card renders `Fallback`.
5. All 9 business / community-space gaps resolve to dedicated art; no card in
   either family renders `Fallback`.
6. A unit-test drift guard over `card-data.csv` asserts AC 1–5 and fails when a
   new card is added without art; `Fallback` remains in the map and resolver for
   genuinely-unknown/future cards (the existing "unknown card" test still passes).
7. Both consumers of `card-art-map.json` (runtime `MainStreetCardArt.ts` and
   `scripts/generate-main-street-card-svgs.mjs`) apply the identical mapping;
   regeneration via `scripts/generate-main-street-card-art.mjs` is
   deterministic and reproducible.
8. `docs/main-street/card-dimensions.md` and `public/assets/CREDITS.md`
   document the mapping rules and the licence/attribution of any new art.
9. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
   comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
10. `npm run build` is green and the **full project test suite must pass** with
    the new changes.

## Constraints

- New art must be permissively licensed (CC0 / MIT / Apache 2.0) and attributed
  in `public/assets/CREDITS.md`.
- Source art remains `sprites/<Name>_1024_x_1024.png`; `card-art-map.json`
  stays generated (never hand-edited).
- No change to the 64×64 zone geometry, the 140×80 card size, the 256×256
  embedded WebP format, or the SVG being self-contained (inline `data:` URI).
- Mapping logic must be expressed once and consumed by both the runtime and the
  static generator.

## Desired artefacts

- Up to 45 new `sprites/<Name>_1024_x_1024.png` source files (9 business /
  community-space, 24 staff, up to 12 event categories) and 39 upgrade
  duplicates named by `newDisplayName`.
- Updated generated mapping + resolver.
- Drift-guard unit test in `tests/main-street/`.
- Docs + credits updates.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetCardArt.ts` — resolver: targetBusiness /
  category resolution or extended alias path.
- `example-games/main-street/card-art-map.json` — regenerated mapping (data).
- `example-games/main-street/scripts/generate-main-street-card-art.mjs` —
  derive the upgrade-duplication and event-category mapping from
  `card-data.csv` + sprites.
- `example-games/main-street/scripts/generate-main-street-card-svgs.mjs` —
  second consumer; mirror the mapping.
- `example-games/main-street/sprites/` — new + duplicated `_1024_x_1024.png`
  source art (producer).
- `tests/main-street/card-art.test.ts` — add the `card-data.csv` drift guard.
- `docs/main-street/card-dimensions.md` — document mapping rules.
- `public/assets/CREDITS.md` — licence/attribution for new art.

## Risks / assumptions

- **Art-availability dependency:** the resolver/tooling can land independently,
  but AC 1–5 cannot pass until the producer's sprites are committed. Plan
  should sequence tooling + drift guard first, art last.
- **Duplicate-name collision (resolved 2026-09-29):** the business `Florist`
  and the event `Community Garden` were renamed to `Flower Shop` and
  `Garden Party` (Q8), so every card name is now unique and no sprite is shared
  across families. IDs are unchanged for save/challenge compatibility.
- **Category-art fidelity (resolved 2026-09-29):** the producer confirmed
  unique (bespoke) art for all 12 event categories, so no representative
  sprite is reused.
- **Dual-consumer drift risk:** `generate-main-street-card-svgs.mjs` duplicates
  the alias logic; a mapping change that misses it silently diverges — assert
  both in tests.
- **Scope-creep risk:** "improve the existing 62 sprites" and "redesign the art
  zone" are out of scope — record separately if they surface.
- **Assumption:** `hasDedicatedCardArt()` remains name-keyed; any targetBusiness
  indirection is baked into the generated map so the public API is unchanged.

## Out of scope

- Changing the 64×64 left-art geometry or the 140×80 card dimensions.
- New card types or `card-data.csv` content changes (beyond `art_notes` if new
  art needs them).
- Filling the empty gameplay `description` column on the 45 `event` rows
  (unrelated to art; all 173 rows already carry `art_notes`).
- Redesigning/replacing the existing 62 dedicated sprites.
- Adding an in-repo image-generation tool (the producer supplies the art).

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- Q1 "Art scope / strategy: how much new art vs. mapping/reuse for the 108
  cards?" — **Answer (producer, 2026-09-26):** Option A — actively duplicate
  the current art using the new name; new art where necessary. Source:
  interactive producer reply.
- Q2 "Art production ownership & pipeline: who produces the new sprites, and
  does this item ship mapping machinery first?" — **Answer (producer,
  2026-09-26):** "I will produce them." Source: interactive producer reply.
  Research: no in-repo sprite generator exists (last sprite commit
  `05026750`, external).
- Q3 "Event mapping granularity: what taxonomy, and is a category sprite
  acceptable for AC4?" — **Answer (producer, 2026-09-26):**
  `trigger` × `targetSynergy` categories. Source: interactive producer reply.
- Q1 prior/open record superseded by the answers above (was OPEN QUESTION).
- Q4 "Source-art size: 64×64 or 1024×1024?" — **Answer (producer,
  2026-09-29):** the producer provides **1024×1024** source art; the 64×64 is
  the on-card display zone. Source: interactive producer reply.
- Q5 "Staff art granularity: per-role or shared?" — **Answer (producer,
  2026-09-29):** **one sprite per role**. Source: interactive producer reply.
- Q6 "Event-category art: reuse a representative or unique?" — **Answer
  (producer, 2026-09-29):** **unique** per category. Source: interactive
  producer reply.
- Q7 "Tighten the drift guard to strict zero-`Fallback` once art lands?" —
  **Answer (producer, 2026-09-29):** **yes**. Source: interactive producer
  reply.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **CG-0MP1QZC6Q005EMEZ** – Asset generation: placeholder SVGs for new cards (completed)
- **CG-0MLTFDAYD0J6KLY3** – Phaser Scene Static Card Layout (completed)
- **CG-0MPD5XALT007F1WV** – Gym Graphics: Card Flip Animation (DeckRng + HandPile) (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` — matched: 0mtorj5fs006b0un, acceptance, add, alias, apache (+136 more)

# Intake brief: Scaffold template must emit `resolve.dedupe` in the generated game-repo `vite.config.ts`

**Type:** chore · **Priority:** medium · **Cross-repo:** yes (`Tableau-Card-Engine` core + this repo) · **Discovered-from:** MS-0MVK3SF54006Y6A6

## Problem statement

`./vite.config.ts` in this repo is AUTO-GENERATED by the core scaffold template `core/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts`, whose banner tells maintainers to edit the template rather than the generated file. MS-0MVK3SF54006Y6A6 fixed a 17-file collection failure by adding `resolve.dedupe: ['phaser', 'tone']` to the *generated* file, but the template still emits only `alias: resolveCoreAliases(coreRoot)` (`core/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts`, `renderViteConfig`). The next `npm run scaffold` therefore silently drops the guard and reintroduces the duplicate-Phaser module-identity split, which only the regression test `tests/tooling/phaser-single-copy.test.ts` would catch — after the fact.

## Users

- **Maintainers/agents who re-scaffold a game repo** — must be able to run `npm run scaffold` without destroying a hand-applied local fix.
  - *User story:* "As a maintainer of tce-main-street, I want `npm run scaffold` to regenerate a `vite.config.ts` that already carries the single-copy guard, so a routine re-scaffold cannot regress the suite."
- **Core template owners** (Tableau-Card-Engine) — must have the guard expressed once, in the template, so every scaffolded game repo starts protected.
  - *User story:* "As a core maintainer, I want `renderViteConfig` to emit the dedupe, so new game repos never hit the 17-file `window is not defined` collection failure."
- **Verification/audit tooling** — full-suite runs in game repos must not fail on a fresh scaffold (audit F3 / pre-push gate).

## Existing state

- `core/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts` → `renderViteConfig(game, coreRel)` emits `resolve: { alias: resolveCoreAliases(coreRoot) }` with no `dedupe`.
- `./vite.config.ts` (this repo, generated) carries `dedupe: ['phaser', 'tone']` plus a long explanatory comment (lines ~160–171), added by MS-0MVK3SF54006Y6A6.
- `core/vite.config.ts` carries the same `dedupe: ['phaser', 'tone']` (core-side rationale: `GAMES_CONFIG=full` distribution builds failed to resolve `phaser` from sibling `src/`, F7 CG-0MUJ168XG006DOGK).
- `tests/tooling/phaser-single-copy.test.ts` guards the **checked-in** config and proves the dedupe is load-bearing; it does not guard the template.
- `core/tests/vite-config.test.ts:100` asserts the core repo's own config dedupes `phaser`/`tone`; `core/tests/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.test.ts` has `describe('renderViteConfig')` (line 352) and `describe('scaffoldGameRepo')` (line 474, real write into a `mkdtemp` fixture).
- This repo's `scaffold` script runs the template **from the `./core` submodule**: `tsx ./core/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts --game main-street --game-repo-root . --core-root ./core` — so the fix reaches this repo only via the submodule pointer.

## Desired change

`renderViteConfig` emits the dedupe immediately after the alias line, with a concise rationale comment (the generated config keeps only a short form of the long local comment, since a re-scaffold rewrites the whole file). The change is authored in the Tableau-Card-Engine repository under its own `CG-…` work item, tested there, committed there, and the `core` submodule pointer here is then bumped to that commit.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Template emits the guard.** `core/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts` → `renderViteConfig` emits `dedupe: ['phaser', 'tone']` immediately after the `alias: resolveCoreAliases(coreRoot)` entry inside the generated `resolve` block, with a short comment stating that shared runtime deps must resolve to exactly one copy (`phaser`, `tone`) and that this mirrors `core/vite.config.ts`.
2. **Template-level test (core).** `core/tests/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.test.ts` → `describe('renderViteConfig')` asserts the emitted source contains the dedupe, and asserts the *placement* contract: the dedupe appears inside the same `resolve: { … }` block, after `resolveCoreAliases(coreRoot)` (a guard that survives reformatting rather than a bare `toContain` on the file text).
3. **On-disk scaffold test (core).** A real `scaffoldGameRepo` run over the temp fixture writes a `vite.config.ts` that contains `dedupe: ['phaser', 'tone']` (assert the written file, not only the rendered string).
4. **Cross-repo provenance.** The change is committed in `/home/rgardler/projects/Tableau-Card-Engine` under a `CG-…` work item, with that repository's build and test gates passing; the `CG-…` id and commit hash are recorded as a comment on this item, and the `core` submodule pointer here is bumped to that commit.
5. **End-to-end proof after the bump.** Scaffolding into a scratch fixture using the bumped submodule template produces a `vite.config.ts` containing the dedupe, and this repo's `tests/tooling/phaser-single-copy.test.ts` still passes unchanged.
6. **Docs.** `docs/dev/testing.md` §"One Phaser copy: `resolve.dedupe` and the `./core` submodule" states that the guard lives in the scaffold template (so a re-scaffold no longer drops it) and names the core-side test that guards the template.
7. **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes** — in the core repository (where the code change lands) and in this repo after the submodule bump.
8. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.

## Constraints

- **Two repositories, two worklogs, two gates.** The edit lands in the `Tableau-Card-Engine` repo (own worklog, own build → test → commit order, own worktree). Do not edit files inside `./core` from this repo's session — only bump the pointer here.
- Only the template + core-side tests + docs change; no behaviour change to this repo's `vite.config.ts` (it already carries the dedupe).
- Do not touch `.pi/`, `skill/`, `command/`, or agent-infrastructure directories.
- Keep the dedupe list exactly `['phaser', 'tone']` — no speculative additions (e.g. adding more shared deps is separate scope).
- No CI/CD pipeline tests.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption (process):** the cross-repo pattern approved in MS-0MUQZH5PH001JXLV (core work item → core commit → submodule bump here) still applies. Evidence: same template function, same two-repo composition, and this repo's `scaffold` script runs `./core/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts`.
- **Assumption (content):** after a re-scaffold the generated `vite.config.ts` replaces the long local rationale comment with the template's shorter one. Behaviour is identical; the long-form explanation in `docs/dev/testing.md` remains the canonical narrative.
- **Risk — silent drift both ways:** the checked-in config and the template can diverge again. Mitigation: the two regression guards (game-repo `phaser-single-copy` test for the config, core scaffold test for the template) plus the docs statement.
- **Risk — submodule bump noise:** bumping `core` may pull in unrelated core commits already on `dev`. Mitigation: bump to the specific commit that carries the template fix and note in the commit message/comment which pointer is landed; if `dev` has moved, land the pointer bump as its own commit.
- **Risk — scope creep:** once the template is open for editing, adjacent "also emit X into the generated config" ideas appear. Record those as separate work items (see `discovered-from` note below), not in this change.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `core/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts` (Tableau-Card-Engine repo) — `renderViteConfig` (~line 314–412): add `dedupe: ['phaser', 'tone']` after the alias line plus rationale comment.
- `core/tests/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.test.ts` (Tableau-Card-Engine repo) — `describe('renderViteConfig')` (line 352) and `describe('scaffoldGameRepo')` (line 474): placement + on-disk assertions.
- `docs/dev/testing.md` — §"One Phaser copy": note the template now carries the guard and the core test that protects it.
- `vite.config.ts` (this repo) — unchanged; reference for the emitted comment text and the dedupe list.
- `core` submodule pointer (`git add core`) — bumped after the core commit.

## Out of scope / discovered

- This repo's `package.json` carries `scaffold:game` / `scaffold:games` scripts pointing at a non-existent `./scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts` (the file lives only in core). Pre-existing, unrelated to this fix, non-blocking — recorded as a separate low-priority chore with `discovered-from:MS-0MVK4TS31000YNFL`.
- Porting the dedupe into the 8 sibling game repos' *checked-in* configs is the sibling concern tracked by MS-0MVBEQ6MC004WRI0 (different repo set, different fix surface).

## Related work

- **MS-0MVK3SF54006Y6A6** (completed, bug) — the 17-file `ReferenceError: window is not defined` collection failure; added the dedupe to this repo's generated config and the `phaser-single-copy` regression test. This item closes the re-scaffold path that would undo it.
- **MS-0MUQZH5PH001JXLV** (completed, task) — precedent: Core scaffold template Pages base — same cross-repo process (CG item in core → core commit → submodule bump), and the same `renderViteConfig` function.
- **MS-0MVBEQ6MC004WRI0** (open, intake_complete) — sibling concern: port the Vite watcher-ignore into sibling game repos' *generated* configs; overlapping family, non-overlapping ACs.
- **MS-0MV8M9IAF000KPNY** (completed, bug) — ENOSPC watcher-exhaustion family (surfaced by the automated related-work report; background only).

## Problem statement

When the street map is visible (roads, road markings, ambient pedestrians and the
city-block grid behind the play area) the translucent market box, the unbounded
player hand row and the semi-transparent HUD strip let that background show
through, so the play surfaces no longer read as distinct sections and the UI is
visually confusing. The bottom band also carries a persistent instruction/hint
line that clutters the hand area, while the "Hint" button surfaces a hint
subsystem that is no longer wanted on the play surface.

## Users

Primary user: the player of Main Street (single-player and human-vs-AI
competitive), playing on the 1280×720 (or expanded) viewport.

Secondary: designers/QA reading the screen at a glance to verify layout, and
developers maintaining the layout contract (SLL zones + tutorial highlight
alignment).

Example user stories:

- As a player, I want the market, player hand and HUD strip to be opaque panels
  like the Activity Log, so that roads and the map grid never bleed through the
  surfaces I am reading and clicking.
- As a player, I want the bottom of the screen to be free of persistent
  instruction text, so that the hand is the lowest, clearest thing on screen.
- As a player, I want my hand cards sitting at the bottom of the screen, so the
  play band feels anchored and I do not have to look above a text line to find
  my cards.
- As a player, when an action is refused (no coins, no hand slot, illegal
  target), I still want the reason shown briefly, so failures never feel silent.
- As a designer, I want the Hint feature gone from the game surface, so the
  play area only offers the controls that are part of the current design.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Market section is opaque.** The market box uses the Activity Log panel
   treatment — fill `0x1a1408` at alpha **0.85** with a 1 px `0x665544` border
   and radius `BOX_RADIUS` — replacing the current `BOX_FILL` alpha 0.3 / stroke
   0.4. Verified by a unit/browser assertion on the market panel graphics style
   (no roads/grid visible through the panel).
2. **Player hand is an opaque panel.** The hand renders on an opaque panel with
   the same Activity Log treatment (fill `0x1a1408` @ 0.85, 1 px `0x665544`
   border, radius), drawn **behind** the hand cards and ghost capacity outlines
   (and above the street/roads layer). The panel covers the full capacity row
   (`maxSlots × (handCardW + 8)`), so it grows/shrinks when `maxHandSize` changes
   (staff hire/lay-off) without clipping cards or ghosts. It is **non-interactive**
   so hand-card clicks, hand→street drag and market→hand drop paths behave exactly
   as before, it survives `refreshPlayerHand`'s `removeAll(true)` rebuild, and it is
   torn down/cleared correctly on scene restart.
3. **HUD strip opacity raised.** The HUD strip fill moves from `0x1a1408` alpha
   0.6 to **0.85** (same stroke token), so the strip matches the other panels.
4. **Persistent instruction/hint line removed.** No `HintBar`/instruction text is
   created, positioned, or updated: `createInstructions` no longer instantiates a
   `HintBar`, `instructionText`/`instructionY` (and every `setText` call site)
   are removed, and no persistent text renders in the bottom band at any phase
   (market, placing-from-hand, event selected, applicant, competitive AI turn).
5. **Hint feature removed end-to-end.** The Hint button is no longer rendered, and
   the hint subsystem is deleted: `src/MainStreetHint.ts`, `onHintClick`,
   `hintUsedThisTurn`, `hintedCardId`/`hintedSlotIndex` (including their per-turn
   resets and market/street hint highlighting), the `'hint'` transcript event
   type, and `hintButtonW` layout plumbing. Hint-specific tests
   (`tests/main-street/hint.test.ts`, `tests/main-street/hint-bar-placement.browser.test.ts`)
   are removed/replaced; the tutorial "banking hint" system is **not** affected
   and its tests keep passing.
6. **Transient feedback preserved.** Messages that previously used the hint line
   (refusals, errors, confirmations such as "Not enough coins…", "Cannot hire…",
   "stays in hand — placement cancelled", "Applied … to slot N") are surfaced as
   short-lived pop text (reusing `@ui` `popTextOrIcon`, reduced-motion aware) and
   remain recorded where they already were in the Activity Log. A representative
   failure path is covered by a test proving the player still gets a visible
   message after the hint line is removed.
7. **Hand anchored at the bottom.** The hand card row's bottom edge sits
   **8–12 px above the viewport bottom** at the 1280×720 base viewport
   (`handY ≈ 628–632`, up from 620), keeping the existing horizontal anchoring
   (left-anchored capacity row centred on the street column,
   `handCenterX = 467`). The hand panel and the ghost outlines move with it, and
   the margin holds on resize/expanded viewports because the position comes from
   the normalised SLL `hand` zone.
8. **Layout contract stays consistent.** `src/layouts/main-street.layout.json`
   `hand` zone and `src/layouts/main-street-tutorial.layout.json` `hand` zone stay
   in sync (tutorial highlight rect must equal the rendered hand rect), the
   documented rects in `MainStreetTutorialHints.ts` and the layout tests
   (`layout-adapter.test.ts`, `tutorial-layout-resolution.test.ts`,
   `TutorialOverlayHighlights.browser.test.ts`) are updated, and the action row
   (End Turn / Peek) keeps its current position — `actionY` must no longer be
   derived from the hand zone — so tutorial highlights and button hit areas do not
   drift.
9. **Regression coverage.** New/updated tests assert: market/hand/HUD panel
   opacity, absence of the Hint button and hint line, hand bottom-margin position,
   hand panel resizing with capacity, and the pop-text feedback replacing the
   instruction line. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes,
   including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries
   (`docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md`, `docs/game/the-build-gdd.md`,
   `docs/dev/ai-strategy.md`, `src/README.md`, `src/scenes/README.md`).
10. **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Constraints

- Positioning comes from the SLL layout authority (`src/layouts/*.json` via
  `computeMainStreetLayoutWithSll()`); no new hard-coded pixel positions.
- Panel styling must reuse existing tokens (`BOX_STROKE`, `BOX_RADIUS`) and the
  Activity Log fill/alpha so the three panels cannot drift.
- `core/` is a submodule (repository boundary): `createMainStreetHintButton` in
  `core/src/ui/Renderer/adapters/MainStreetAdapter.ts` becomes unused after this
  change — file a follow-up core work item rather than editing the submodule here.
- Tutorial hint/banking-hint systems are out of scope and must keep working.
- Do not edit `.pi/`, `skill/`, `command/` or other agent infrastructure.
- CHANGELOG.md is managed by the release pipeline and is excluded.

## Existing state

- **Activity Log** (reference style): `0x1a1408` @ 0.85 fill, 1 px `0x665544`
  border, `LOG_TITLE_H` title bar — `MainStreetRendererStreet.ts:286-317`.
  Challenge tracker and Upcoming queue share the same treatment.
- **Market box**: `BOX_FILL` (`0x2a1f14`) @ 0.3, stroke 0.4 —
  `MainStreetRendererMarket.ts:52-60`.
- **HUD strip**: `0x1a1408` @ 0.6 rectangle — `MainStreetRendererHud.ts:239-245`.
- **Player hand**: no background panel at all; `HandView` draws cards + ghost
  capacity outlines directly over the scene at `handY = 0.861111 × 720 = 620`
  (`MainStreetRendererStreet.ts:78-120`, `MainStreetLayoutAdapter.ts`).
- **Instruction line**: shared `HintBar` created in `createInstructions`
  (`MainStreetRendererHud.ts:78-88`), repositioned to
  `(logX/2, handY − 20)` = `(480, 600)` on resize/refresh
  (`MainStreetLifecycleManagerLifecycle.ts:719-721`); 137 references across 11
  source files push phase instructions, errors and confirmations through it.
- **Hint feature**: `src/MainStreetHint.ts` (`generateHint` → Greedy AI move +
  rationale), invoked from `onHintClick` (`MainStreetInputManager.ts:229-269`),
  which sets `hintUsedThisTurn` and `hintedCardId`/`hintedSlotIndex`; the button
  is rendered by `createMainStreetHintButton` (`MainStreetRendererHud.ts:529-542`)
  using `layout.hintButtonW`; the action is also recorded as a `'hint'`
  transcript event and an Activity Log line.
- Road/map rendering (`drawStreetRoads`, `MainStreetRendererStreet.ts:417+`) is
  confined to the masked street viewport, but translucent panels elsewhere still
  let the map backdrop read through when the camera is zoomed/panned.

## Desired change

Three bottom/top play surfaces read as solid, self-contained sections in the
Activity Log style; the bottom band carries no persistent instruction text; the
player hand sits at the very bottom of the screen on its own opaque panel; the
Hint button and hint subsystem are gone; and refusals/confirmations still reach
the player as brief pop text plus Activity Log entries.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererMarket.ts` — Market box fill alpha 0.3 → 0.85
  (Activity Log treatment).
- `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererHud.ts` — HUD strip alpha 0.6 → 0.85; remove
  `createInstructions`/`HintBar` wiring, Hint button creation and phase-specific
  `hintBar.setText(...)` blocks; compute the action row's leftmost x without
  `hintButtonW`.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererStreet.ts` — add the persistent opaque hand panel
  behind the hand cards (sized from the capacity row), keep ghost outlines on top;
  drop `hintedSlotIndex` highlights.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererLayout.ts` — `refreshPlayerHand` keeps the panel in
  sync with `maxHandSize`.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetInputManager.ts` — delete `onHintClick`; pop-text feedback
  for hint-line messages.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnController*.ts`, `src/scenes/MainStreetScene.ts`,
  `src/scenes/MainStreetLifecycleManagerLifecycle.ts`,
  `src/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts` — remove `instructionText`/`hintBar`/
  hint-state call sites and resets; route feedback to pop text + log.
- `src/layouts/main-street.layout.json`, `src/layouts/main-street-tutorial.layout.json`
  — `hand` zone y moved to the bottom margin (628/720 ≈ 0.872222), kept in sync.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetLayoutAdapter.ts`, `src/scenes/MainStreetConstants.ts` —
  remove `instructionY`/`hintButtonW`; decouple `actionY` from the hand zone.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetTutorialHints.ts` — update the documented hand rect.
- `src/MainStreetHint.ts` — **delete** (hint subsystem).
- `src/MainStreetTranscript.ts` — remove the `'hint'` event variant.
- `src/MainStreetAiStrategy.ts` — comment clean-up where hints are described as a
  consumer of the Greedy strategy.
- `tests/main-street/hint.test.ts`, `tests/main-street/hint-bar-placement.browser.test.ts`
  — delete/replace with tests asserting the hint line/button are gone.
- `tests/main-street/layout-adapter.test.ts`, `tests/main-street/tutorial-layout-resolution.test.ts`,
  `tests/main-street/TutorialOverlayHighlights.browser.test.ts`,
  `tests/main-street/TutorialOverlayManager.browser.test.ts`,
  `tests/main-street/hud-strip-layout.browser.test.ts`,
  plus the ~46 `instructionText` assertions across
  `tests/main-street/*.test.ts` — update to the new layout/feedback contract.
- `docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md`, `docs/game/the-build-gdd.md`,
  `docs/dev/ai-strategy.md`, `src/README.md`, `src/scenes/README.md` — document
  opaque panels, bottom-anchored hand, removed hint system, and the new feedback
  channel.

## Related work

- **MS-0MUMP96XH002SJ89** (completed) — named storylines / outcome feedback &
  continuity indicator: established the current bottom-band HUD feedback patterns.
- **MS-0MTIIKVJE006GRQY** (completed) — competitive state model: per-player
  resources, owner-tagged street (hand/HUD panels must stay legible in competitive
  mode).
- **MS-0MUTU8J9T0034OT7** (completed) — competitive scoreboard & active-seat HUD
  (same HUD strip that gains the 0.85 opacity).
- Automated relation report (find-related skill) for this item records the
  repository matches: `core/docs/DEVELOPER.md` (hand/HUD panel semantics),
  `core/CHANGELOG.md`, and `core/docs/the-build/genre-research.md` (HUD/opaque
  panel guidance) — all read-only references for this change.
- Related docs: `docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md` (§ Player hand layout, undo/redo
  pop "above the hint bar"), `docs/game/the-build-gdd.md` (§ AI Strategy and Hint
  System), `docs/dev/ai-strategy.md`, `docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md` (worktree
  rules).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Input-interception risk.** A full-width background rectangle behind the hand
  would sit over the bottom band; if made interactive it silently swallows hand
  clicks and drag targets. It must be non-interactive (`setInteractive` never
  called) and rendered below the cards, verified by the existing hand click/drag
  browser tests.
- **Legacy transcript tolerance.** Removing the `'hint'` transcript variant only
  affects the TypeScript union; saved transcripts containing historical hint
  events are read tolerantly (replay adapters accept unknown event shapes), so no
  data migration is needed — the assumption is recorded, not silently made.

- **Removing the hint system removes a player-assist feature.** Producer explicitly
  chose full removal (Q5 = C); the GDD § *AI Strategy and Hint System* becomes
  design intent only and must say the feature is not currently surfaced.
- **Silent-failure risk.** ~46 tests and many code paths use the removed text as
  the only failure message; the pop-text channel must keep every refusal visible
  (AC6), otherwise illegal moves read as unresponsive.
- **Layout drift risk.** The tutorial highlight contract pins the hand rect; moving
  the hand without updating `main-street-tutorial.layout.json` breaks highlight
  alignment. `actionY` is currently derived from `handY`, so decoupling it is
  required to keep End Turn/Peek hit areas and highlights stable.
- **Capacity growth risk.** Staff can raise `maxHandSize` beyond 3; a fixed-width
  hand panel would clip cards or ghost outlines. The panel must size from the
  capacity row and update on hire/lay-off.
- **Scope creep.** While touching panels, resist restyling the street slots,
  challenge tracker or Upcoming queue (already 0.85) — record any further visual
  opportunities as separate work items.
- **Assumption.** "Opaque like the Activity Log" means the Activity Log's existing
  0.85 alpha + border + radius (not alpha 1.0), so all panels share one token set.
- **Assumption.** Hand horizontal anchoring is unchanged (left-anchored capacity
  row centred on the street column); only the vertical position changes.
- **Assumption.** `createMainStreetHintButton` lives in the `core` submodule and is
  left in place (unused) with a follow-up core work item, per repository
  boundaries.

## Open Questions

None — all five interview questions were answered by the producer.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1. Scope of the opaque treatment — which surfaces?**
  - Options: (a) market + hand only; (b) market + hand + HUD strip; (c) every
    translucent surface.
  - **Recommended:** (a) — matches the seed wording, minimal change.
  - **Answer (producer, interactive reply):** **(b)** — market panel, player hand
    panel *and* HUD strip at 0.85.
- **Q2. "Remove the hint text" — what exactly?**
  - Options: (a) remove the bottom-centre instruction line, keep the Hint button;
    (b) remove the instruction line *and* the Hint button; (c) other.
  - **Recommended:** (a) — the line is the clutter; the button is functional.
  - **Answer (producer, interactive reply):** **(b)** — remove the instruction
    line and the Hint button.
- **Q3. Hand destination.**
  - Options: (a) straight down to an 8–12 px bottom margin keeping current
    horizontal anchoring; (b) also re-centre horizontally; (c) other margin.
  - **Recommended:** (a) — simple and preserves street alignment.
  - **Answer (producer, interactive reply):** **(a)** — card bottoms 8–12 px from
    the viewport bottom, horizontal anchoring unchanged.
- **Q4. The removed hint line is also the error/feedback channel — what replaces
  it?**
  - Options: (a) transient pop/toast (`popTextOrIcon`) + keep Activity Log entries;
    (b) a one-line message area that only renders while a message is live;
    (c) drop text feedback entirely (shake + SFX only).
  - **Recommended:** (a) — keeps failures visible without reintroducing clutter.
  - **Research:** transient messaging already exists via `@ui` `popTextOrIcon`
    ("Undid: …" rides above the bottom band, `docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md:1015`);
    Activity Log already records outcomes.
  - **Answer (producer, interactive reply):** **(a)**.
- **Q5. What happens to the hint *system* once the "Hint" button goes?**
  - Options: (a) remove the button only, keep `generateHint` + tests; (b) rebind to
    a keyboard shortcut; (c) remove the hint system code and tests entirely.
  - **Recommended:** (a) — surgical, per "mention dead code, don't delete it".
  - **Answer (producer, interactive reply):** **(c)** — remove the hint subsystem
    and its tests as part of this item.
  - **Research:** hint code is self-contained — `src/MainStreetHint.ts`
    (`generateHint`, `buildRationale`), `onHintClick` in `MainStreetInputManager`,
    `hintedCardId`/`hintedSlotIndex` highlighting in the market and street
    renderers, the `'hint'` transcript variant, and
    `tests/main-street/hint.test.ts`; the tutorial banking-hint system is
    unrelated and stays.

## Plan (feature decomposition)

Decomposed into **9 child work items**, created test-first. Four test-contract
items (each blocking its paired implementation item) define the red tests;
four implementation items ship code + tests + local code comments; one docs
item consolidates the cross-repo documentation. Each implementation slice is a

# Bank Loans

A player (human or AI) who cannot pay their end-of-turn costs can take a bank loan
instead of going bankrupt: a fixed principal is credited immediately and repaid as a
fixed per-turn amount (principal + 10% total interest) until the term expires. Loans
cost no action point and there is at most one active loan per player.

## Problem statement

Bankruptcy is currently a terminal state (`checkImmediateLoss` fires at `coins < 0`,
`resolveCompetitiveSeatFailures` eliminates an AI seat), so a single bad week ends a
run with no recovery path. Players also have no way to convert future income into
present cash, which narrows strategic options in the mid-game. Bank Loans add a
credit mechanic that lets a player buy their way past a cash crunch at the cost of a
fixed debt burden.

## Users

- **Human player (single- and competitive mode)** — "When my end-of-turn costs leave
  me at negative coins, I want to be offered a loan so I can keep playing instead of
  losing the run."
- **Human player, mid-game** — "When I am short of the cash for a strong move at the
  end of a turn, I want to borrow a fixed amount with a repayment schedule I can see,
  so I can judge whether the debt is worth it."
- **AI opponent (competitive mode)** — "When I go bankrupt I should be given the same
  bailout a human gets, so an unlucky week does not knock me out of the game."

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Loan offer & taking a loan.** A seat with no active loan can take a loan by choosing one option from the configured loan menu (default: 300 coins / 3 turns, 600 / 6, 1000 / 10). Taking a loan credits the principal to that seat's wallet immediately, records the active loan, and **costs no action point** (`actionsRemaining` unchanged).
2. **One active loan per player.** A seat that already has an active loan cannot take or accept another one; the attempt is rejected with a clear, user-facing reason and no resource change.
3. **Fixed per-turn repayment.** At the end of every turn in which a seat holds an active loan, exactly `perTurnRepayment` coins are deducted from that seat's wallet (`totalRepayment = round(principal × 1.10)`, `perTurnRepayment = round(totalRepayment / termTurns)`; e.g. 600 / 6 → 110 per turn, 660 total). The deduction is recorded in the turn's net summary as a one-off expense; the loan is retired after `termTurns` payments and no further deductions occur.
4. **Bankruptcy bailout.** When a seat would fail on `coins < 0` (single-player loss, or competitive seat failure) **and holds no active loan**, the game does not end (and the seat is not eliminated): a loan offer is presented instead. Accepting credits the principal and play continues; declining, or already holding an active loan, preserves today's bankruptcy behaviour. At most one bailout offer is made per seat per turn (no offer loop).
5. **AI bailout policy.** An AI seat that hits `coins < 0` with no active loan auto-accepts the **largest** loan option and is not eliminated; an AI seat that already holds an active loan is eliminated exactly as today. AI seats take no proactive (non-bailout) loans.
6. **Visible obligation.** While a loan is active the player can see what they owe: the activity log records the loan (amount, per-turn repayment, term) and the remaining obligation (turns left + per-turn amount) is surfaced in the HUD, so the debt burden is never hidden.
7. **Repayment shortfall.** Repayment is deducted unconditionally, so a payment that exceeds the seat's balance leaves `coins < 0` and triggers the normal bankruptcy path — which offers a bailout only if the seat has no active loan (per AC4), i.e. a seat already repaying a loan simply goes bankrupt.
8. **Headless determinism.** Headless turn execution (`endTurnHeadless`, Monte Carlo, balance runs) never stalls on a pending loan offer: it resolves deterministically using the AC5 AI policy, and simulations without loans enabled are byte-identical to today's results.
9. **Persistence and back-compatibility.** Active loans and a pending offer survive a save/load round-trip; pre-loan saves (schema v2) load with no loans and unchanged behaviour. Save schema version is bumped with a migration.
10. **Testing/validation.** New unit tests cover the loan maths (option table, `perTurnRepayment`, retirement after `termTurns`), single-loan enforcement, bailout offer/accept/decline, shortfall → bankruptcy, AI largest-option policy, headless resolution and save/load round-trip; the competitive-seat path is covered by an integration test.
11. **Documentation.** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, `docs/game/core-rules-and-mechanics.md`, and the in-game help content where it lists end-of-turn economy rules.
12. **Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **No action point cost** — taking a loan must not decrement `actionsRemaining`
  (seed requirement).
- **Fixed menu, no negotiation** — the loan menu is configuration data
  (`config.loanOptions`), identical for every seat in a run; no per-seat or
  per-difficulty negotiation UI. Re-balancing is a config edit only.
- **Interest model** — flat 10% of principal over the whole term, spread evenly
  (`600 / 6 → 110/week`, per the seed's worked example). No compounding, no
  per-turn-on-outstanding-balance interest.
- **One active loan per player** (producer decision Q1 = A) — no debt stacking.
- **Bailout-only AI** (Q3 = A) — AI strategy changes are limited to auto-accepting a
  bailout offer; no new AI heuristics otherwise.
- **Economy realism** — repayment moves through the existing `EconomyLedger` /
  `resourceBank` sync path; no direct wallet mutation.
- **Config defaults** — `loansEnabled: true` in the `Easy`/`Medium`/`Hard` presets
  (the mechanic is live in the game), and `false` for headless/simulation configs so
  existing Monte Carlo and balance baselines stay unchanged until a simulation opts in.
- **No turn-summary dependency** — the Turn Summary dialog
  (MS-0MVL6HMDP004WI41) does not exist yet; this item must not block on it.

## Existing state

- Bankruptcy is terminal and evaluated in two places:
  `checkImmediateLoss` (single-player, `coins < 0` → `endReason 'bankruptcy'`) and
  `resolveCompetitiveSeatFailures` (competitor seats; human → loss, AI →
  `eliminateCompetitiveSeat`), both in `src/MainStreetEngineTurnClosing.ts`.
  An opening-day grace already exists (`applyFirstSharedDaySolvencyGrace`,
  MS-0MVJNFESC005QJ41), which bailout evaluation must respect.
- Pending-decision pausing is an established pattern: `state.pendingEventChoice` and
  `state.pendingPiggyback` both defer the closing tail and are resolved by the UI
  before the closing re-runs — a pending loan offer should follow the same shape.
- Turn economy closes in `processEndOfTurn` (income, ongoing costs, incident) and
  summarises into the activity log via `appendTurnNetRow`; a repayment expense belongs
  in that same sequence so the net row reflects it.
- Per-seat wallets live in `state.players[].coins` (competitive) while
  `state.resourceBank` is the working mirror bound by `bindCompetitiveSeat` /
  `restoreCompetitiveSeat`; `state.players` is `undefined` in single-player.
- `GameConfig` (`src/MainStreetDifficulty.ts`) is a numeric-parameter bag derived from
  difficulty presets, consumed by the engine — the natural home for loan config.
- No loan code exists anywhere in the repo (`grep -ri loan src core tests docs` is
  empty) — this is net-new capability.
- Save/load uses `serializeMainStreetState` / `deserializeMainStreetState` with a
  strict schema-version check (`MAIN_STREET_SAVE_SCHEMA_VERSION = 2`) and a migration
  hook, so a version bump plus defaults is the established path for new fields.

## Desired change

1. **Loan model** — new `LoanOption` / `ActiveLoan` types and `MainStreetLoans.ts`
   holding the option table, offer computation, and pure apply/resolve helpers.
   State gains `loans: ActiveLoan[]` (invariant: at most one entry per `ownerId`) and
   `pendingLoanOffer?: { ownerId, reason, options }`.
2. **Config** — `loansEnabled`, `loanInterestRate` (0.10) and `loanOptions` added to
   `GameConfig` and all difficulty presets (`loansEnabled: true`); headless/simulation
   configs default it to `false` so existing balance baselines are unchanged.
3. **Taking a loan** — a `takeLoan` command (no AP cost) validated against the
   one-active-loan rule, crediting principal via the ledger and logging the decision.
4. **Repayment** — `applyLoanRepayments(state)` invoked in the closing sequence ahead
   of the end-condition checks, decrementing `turnsRemaining` and logging the expense
   into the turn net row.
5. **Bailout offer** — `maybeOfferBailout(state)` evaluated *before* the bankruptcy /
   seat-failure declarations: when a seat with no active loan is at `coins < 0`, set
   `pendingLoanOffer` (reason `bankruptcy`) and pause the closing instead of ending the
   game; `acceptLoanOffer` / `declineLoanOffer` resume it. Declining, a second offer in
   the same turn, or an already-active loan preserves current behaviour.
6. **Visible obligation** — log the loan at acceptance and surface
   "Loan: X coins/turn, N turns left" in the HUD beside the coin/reputation readouts.
7. **UI** — a bailout overlay (option list with per-turn and total repayment shown,
   plus Decline) rendered when a pending offer exists, wiring the deferred-closing
   resume path in `MainStreetTurnController`. The mid-game entry point on the Turn
   Summary dialog is **out of scope** here (see Non-goals).
8. **AI** — bailout auto-accept of the largest option in the AI/headless path.
9. **Persistence** — serialise `loans` and `pendingLoanOffer`; bump the save schema to
   v3 with a migration defaulting legacy saves to an empty loan list.

### Non-goals / out of scope

- Wiring the "Bank Loan" button into the Turn Summary dialog
  (MS-0MVL6HMDP004WI41) — a thin follow-up once that dialog lands. Per producer
  decision Q4, **if the dialog is not completed in time, raise a separate follow-up
  work item** for the wiring rather than expanding this item.
- Multiple concurrent/stacked loans, variable or negotiated interest, per-seat credit
  limits.
- Deducting outstanding principal from the score, or any loan effect on reputation.
- Proactive (non-bailout) AI loan strategy.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/MainStreetLoans.ts` — **new**. Option table (`DEFAULT_LOAN_OPTIONS`), repayment
  maths, `takeLoan`, `applyLoanRepayments`, `maybeOfferBailout`,
  `acceptLoanOffer` / `declineLoanOffer`, active-loan lookup per owner.
- `src/MainStreetStateTypes.ts` — `LoanOption`, `ActiveLoan`, `PendingLoanOffer`
  types; `loans` and `pendingLoanOffer` fields on `MainStreetState`.
- `src/MainStreetDifficulty.ts` — `loansEnabled`, `loanInterestRate`, `loanOptions` on
  `GameConfig` plus all presets (`Easy`/`Medium`/`Hard`).
- `src/MainStreetEngineTurnClosing.ts` — call `applyLoanRepayments` and
  `maybeOfferBailout` ahead of `checkImmediateLoss` / `checkEndConditions` /
  `resolveCompetitiveSeatFailures`; defer the closing tail while an offer is pending.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererHud.ts` — active-loan readout (turns left,
  per-turn repayment) beside the coin/reputation HUD.
- `src/MainStreetHelpContent.ts` — end-of-turn economy help text: loan menu and
  bailout rule.
- `src/MainStreetEngineTypes.ts` — `pendingLoanOffer` on `TurnResult` (mirroring
  `choicePending` / `piggybackPending`) and a `TakeLoanAction` in `PlayerAction`.
- `src/MainStreetEngineCommands.ts`, `src/MainStreetCommands.ts` — `takeLoan` handler
  and command dispatch; assert no AP consumption.
- `src/MainStreetAiStrategy.ts` — bailout auto-accept (largest option) for AI seats.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetLoanOverlay.ts` — **new**. Bailout dialog: option rows with
  per-turn/total repayment, Accept and Decline.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnController.ts`, `src/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts`,
  `src/scenes/MainStreetGameOverSummary.ts` — show the overlay instead of the game-over
  summary while a bailout offer is open; resume the deferred closing on resolution.
- `src/MainStreetStateSerialize.ts`, `src/MainStreetSaveLoad.ts` — serialise/restore
  loans and the pending offer; bump `MAIN_STREET_SAVE_SCHEMA_VERSION` to 3 with a
  migration.
- `src/MainStreetMonteCarlo.ts` — headless deterministic resolution of a pending offer.
- `tests/main-street/MainStreetLoans.test.ts` — **new**. Maths, one-loan rule, config.
- `tests/main-street/MainStreetLoanBailout.test.ts` — **new**. Bailout offer/accept/
  decline, shortfall, AI policy, headless.
- `tests/main-street/MainStreetLoanSaveLoad.test.ts` — **new**. Round-trip + v2
  migration.
- `docs/game/core-rules-and-mechanics.md` — economy section: loan menu, repayment
  schedule, bailout rule.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption — interest arithmetic.** The seed's worked example (600 over 6 turns at
  110/turn = 660 total) is read as "10% of principal over the whole term, spread
  evenly", not "10% per turn on the outstanding balance" (which would be ~137/turn).
  Low risk: the example is unambiguous arithmetic; a config-driven `loanInterestRate`
  makes the alternative a one-line change.
- **Assumption — default option menu.** Three options (300/3, 600/6, 1000/10) all
  yielding 110/turn are proposed so the producer's choice (Q2 = B, "a choice among
  options") has a concrete, balanced default. Pure config data; re-balancing needs no
  code change.
- **Assumption — loans do not affect scoring.** Debt only drains coins; outstanding
  principal is not deducted from `finalScore`. Recorded as a possible follow-up rather
  than scope.
- **Risk — end-condition ordering.** The bailout intercept must run *before*
  `checkImmediateLoss` / `resolveCompetitiveSeatFailures`, and must respect the
  existing first-turn solvency grace, or the game will end before the offer is shown.
  Mitigation: explicit ordering tests plus a per-turn "already offered" guard.
- **Risk — deferred closing loops.** Reusing the `pendingLoanOffer` pause means the
  closing can be re-entered; an unresolvable offer (decline with no other option) must
  converge to game over in one pass. Mitigation: idempotency tests and the per-turn
  offer guard.
- **Risk — headless/Monte Carlo regressions.** A pending offer that blocks headless
  closing would hang balance runs. Mitigation: AC7 determinism tests plus
  `loansEnabled: false` default for simulation configs, with before/after result
  comparison.
- **Risk — save schema.** Bumping the shared save schema risks older-campaign
  compatibility. Mitigation: v2 migration test that loads a pre-loan save unchanged.
- **Risk — scope creep.** The Turn Summary dialog entry point, proactive AI lending and
  score effects are natural "while we're here" additions; each is recorded as a
  non-goal/follow-up rather than absorbed into this item.

## Related work

- **MS-0MVL6HMDP004WI41 — End of Turn summary** (stage `idea`). Defines the
  turn-summary dialog with a "Bank Loan" button that is explicitly waiting on this
  feature. **Related, not blocking**: this item ships the engine, bailout flow and
  `takeLoan` command without it; the dialog wiring is a follow-up (see Non-goals).
- **MS-0MUWE6MSQ006DEZ4 — End-reason & player-state model** (completed). Introduced the
  `EndReason` union (`bankruptcy`, `reputation_collapse`, …) and the per-seat failure
  badges that the bailout path intercepts.
- **MS-0MUVQRBVI0015AB2 — AI seat elimination / last standing** (completed via
  `eliminateCompetitiveSeat`, `checkLastStanding`). The bailout must run before
  elimination so an AI survives, which in turn delays last-standing wins.
- **MS-0MVJNFESC005QJ41 — Play Again does not reset the AI** (completed). Also
  introduced the opening-day solvency grace (`applyFirstSharedDaySolvencyGrace`) that
  bailout evaluation must respect.
- **MS-0MUWDL0V40041USM — Provide reason for game ending** (completed). Game-over
  copy/end-reason surfacing that the "declined bailout" path must still produce.
- **MS-0MUYC47EL005Z69H / CG-0MTSHG8RP008E128 — pending-decision pausing**
  (`pendingEventChoice`, `pendingPiggyback`). The `pendingLoanOffer` pause should
  follow this established deferred-closing pattern.
- Duplicate check performed — no completed item covers bank loans; the only overlap is
  the turn-summary dialog item above (partial relationship, not a duplicate).

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

Round 1

- **Q1: Can a player hold more than one loan at once?**
  — Answer (producer, interactive reply): **A — one active loan per player; further
  offers deferred until it is repaid.** Source: interactive reply, session
  `herdr-1792944777-2932233-30937`.
- **Q2: What shape is the loan offer?**
  — Answer (producer, interactive reply): **B — a choice among options (e.g. 300/3,
  600/6), pick one.** Source: interactive reply, same session. Consequence: the brief
  defines a config-driven option menu rather than a single fixed offer.
- **Q3: How do AI opponents use loans?**
  — Answer (producer, interactive reply): **A — bankruptcy bailout only; auto-accept
  when an AI seat hits `coins < 0`.** Source: interactive reply, same session.
  Consequence: no proactive AI lending in this item.

Round 2

- **Q4: Entry point while the Turn Summary dialog does not exist yet?**
  — Answer (producer, interactive reply): **A — build the loan engine + `takeLoan`
  command + bankruptcy-bailout UI now; wire the Turn-summary "Bank Loan" button when
  that dialog lands, and create a follow-up item if the dialog has not been completed
  in time.** Source: interactive reply, same session.
- **Q5: Which option does an AI auto-accept on bailout?**
  — Answer (producer, interactive reply): **A — the largest available option.** Source:
  interactive reply, same session.
- **Q6: Repayment shortfall behaviour?**
  — Answer (producer, interactive reply): **A — deduct anyway; negative coins trigger
  the existing bankruptcy flow, and a seat that already holds a loan gets no new
  offer.** Source: interactive reply, same session.

Research notes: repo searched for existing loan code (`grep -ri loan src core tests
docs` — no matches) and for the bankruptcy hooks (`checkImmediateLoss`,
`resolveCompetitiveSeatFailures`, `applyFirstSharedDaySolvencyGrace`). Related

# `implement.py phase_start` records the worktree as `repo_root` on resume-from-worktree

discovered-from:MS-0MVLINWHE004W4CP

## Problem statement

`phase_start` resolves the main checkout root correctly at Step 6.5
(`repo_root = _get_repo_root() or ...`) but then **recomputes it from
`Path.cwd()` at Step 8** and writes that value into
`.implement_state.json`. When `start` is run as a resume from inside an
existing worktree — the normal driven-child pattern — `cwd` *is* the
worktree, so the state file records the worktree as `repo_root` and every
downstream consumer of that value is wrong: `phase_finish` cannot fast-forward
`dev` in the main checkout, and its worktree-removal gate refuses to remove
"the repository root", so a successfully pushed implementation is left
stranded with the work item reset to `open`.

## Users

- **Agent-implementer** resuming a driven child session or re-running `start`
  in an existing worktree: needs `start` → `finish` to work unchanged, with no
  manual state-file surgery.
- **Parent/phase session** orchestrating children: a stranded child leaves the
  parent phase unable to close the epic and burns a session on recovery.
- **Maintainer** reading `.implement_state.json`: needs `repo_root` to mean one
  thing — the main checkout — so state is diagnosable.

Example user stories:

> As a driven child session resuming its worktree, I want `implement.py start`
> to record the main checkout root, so that `finish` can fast-forward `dev`
> and remove my worktree.

> As a parent session, I want a child that already has a bad state file to
> still finish cleanly, so that I do not have to hand-edit JSON to unblock an
> epic.

## Existing state

`skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` (source repo `SorraAgents`; the global
install `~/.pi/agent/skills` is a symlink to `SorraAgents/skill`):

| Line (at `91de33cf5`) | Code | Role |
|---|---|---|
| 4110 | `repo_root = _get_repo_root() or str(Path.cwd().resolve())` | Step 6.5 — correct main-root resolution (used for the parent-branch refresh) |
| 4178 | `repo_root = str(Path.cwd().resolve())` | **Defect** — Step 8 overwrites the correct value before `_store_signal_globals` / `write_state` |
| 4613-4616 | `repo_root = state.repo_root if state else (...)` | `phase_finish` trusts the (wrong) state value for the `dev` fast-forward, the push and `_sync_parent_branch` |
| 4732 | `_remove_worktree(worktree_path, repo_root=state.repo_root if state else None)` | Gate 1 compares `worktree_path.resolve()` with `repo_root.resolve()` → `RuntimeError: REFUSE to remove the repository root` |
| 4872 | `repo_root = str(Path.cwd().resolve())` | `phase_abort` Step 3 — same defect class: `_restore_repo_state` runs `git checkout dev` / `git pull` in the worktree, both silently failing (`check=False`) |

Failure sequence observed (resume-from-worktree start):

1. `start` writes `repo_root = <worktree>`; `_store_signal_globals` gets the
   same value, so the SIGTERM handler's `_restore_repo_state` would also run in
   the worktree.
2. `finish` Step 5 tries `git checkout dev` inside the worktree → fails ("already
   checked out"); caught and logged as a warning, so the main checkout is never
   fast-forwarded (the pre-push context-budget gate then works from a stale
   checkout).
3. `finish` Step 6 pushes successfully from the worktree, **then** Step 7 calls
   `_remove_worktree(worktree_path, repo_root=<worktree>)`, which raises the
   safety-gate `RuntimeError`; the outer handler resets the item to `open`,
   posts no completion comment, and leaves the worktree in place.
4. The worktree can then be removed by a later cleanup pass (signal handler /
   parent phase) **while the child session's `cwd` is still inside it** — the
   reported end state: a session stranded on a deleted working directory.
   `_remove_worktree` deliberately `chdir`s to `repo_root` before removal, but
   with the wrong `repo_root` stored it either raises before that `chdir` or
   chdirs into the worktree it is about to delete.

Live evidence of the same defect (recorded during this intake, not fixed here):

```
.worklog/worktrees/wl-SA-0MVLJWL60001H6QK-drive-timeout-reconciliation-test-suite/.implement_state.json
  "repo_root": ".../.worklog/worktrees/wl-SA-0MVLJWL60001H6QK-drive-timeout-reconciliation-test-suite"
  "started_at": "2026-10-24T11:11:45Z"
```

(SA-0MVLJWL60001H6QK — Drive timeout-reconciliation test suite — is still
`open`/`intake_complete`; that worktree is the recovery target, not scope of
this item.)

## Desired change

1. **Fix the source of truth.** Make Step 8 use the already-resolved main
   checkout root (reuse the Step 6.5 value / call `_get_repo_root()`), so
   `_store_signal_globals` and the state file always carry the main checkout,
   never the worktree.
2. **Repair stale state defensively.** In `phase_finish` and `phase_abort`,
   treat a `state.repo_root` that resolves to the worktree itself (or to a path
   inside it) as stale and fall back to `_get_repo_root(worktree_path)`; keep
   the correct value for the remaining steps (and, optionally, rewrite the
   state file). This is what unblocks worktrees already stranded by the bug
   **without** hand-editing JSON.
3. **Fix the abort path.** `phase_abort` Step 3 must restore the *main*
   checkout when invoked from inside the worktree.
4. **Regress-proof it.** A test that fails on the pre-fix code: a real
   temporary git repo plus a linked worktree, `cwd` set inside the worktree,
   `start` resumed, asserting the persisted `repo_root` is the main root; plus a
   finish-gate assertion that the worktree path is never handed to
   `_remove_worktree` as `repo_root`.

## Implementation plan (test-first)

Ordered so the regression test lands **first** and is proven to fail before
the fix (test-first ordering per the implement skill):

1. **Test (red).** New `skill/implement/tests/test_repo_root_resolution.py`
   using a real `tmp_path` git repo (`git init`, one commit on `dev`) plus a
   linked worktree (`git worktree add`), with no `_get_repo_root` mocking:
   - `cwd` inside the worktree, `phase_start` resumed → `.implement_state.json`
     `repo_root` is the main checkout root and the value handed to
     `_store_signal_globals` matches it;
   - a state file whose `repo_root` is the worktree itself → `phase_finish`'s
     worktree-removal gate succeeds and the worktree path is never passed to
     `_remove_worktree` as `repo_root`;
   - `phase_abort` run from inside the worktree leaves the **main** checkout on
     the parent branch (and behaves identically when run from the main
     checkout).
   Confirm all three fail against the pre-fix code, then keep them passing.
2. **Fix Step 8.** Reuse the already-resolved Step 6.5 `repo_root`
   (`_get_repo_root()`), removing the `Path.cwd()` recomputation, so
   `_store_signal_globals` and `write_state` always carry the main checkout.
3. **Harden `phase_finish`.** Treat a `state.repo_root` equal to, or inside,
   `worktree_path` as stale: log the rejected and derived values at WARNING
   and derive the main root with `_get_repo_root(worktree_path)` (falling back
   to discovery), then use it for the `dev` fast-forward, the push,
   `_sync_parent_branch` and the `_remove_worktree` call.
   `_remove_worktree`'s own gates stay untouched.
4. **Fix `phase_abort` Step 3.** Apply the same stale-state rejection, then
   `_restore_repo_state(main_root)` so `git checkout`/`pull` run in the main
   checkout instead of silently failing inside the worktree.
5. **Docs.** State-file schema note — `repo_root` is always the **main
   checkout** — in `skill/implement/SKILL.md` and
   `docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md`, plus code comments at each corrected
   site.
6. **Verify.** Changed-scope test run then full suite via `/skill:test`;
   commit → push on the SorraAgents `dev` branch (this repo only).

Between steps: re-read the next step's description before starting it; if a
step reveals a further `Path.cwd()`-derived repo root, file it as a linked
work item rather than widening this fix (see Risks).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] After a fresh `start` **and** a resume-from-worktree `start` (cwd inside
      `.worklog/worktrees/wl-<id>-…`), the written `.implement_state.json`
      records `repo_root` as the main checkout root (`git rev-parse
      --git-common-dir`'s parent), never the worktree path; the same value is
      passed to `_store_signal_globals`.
- [ ] `phase_finish` treats a stale `state.repo_root` equal to (or inside) the
      worktree as invalid and derives the main root from the worktree, so the
      worktree-removal gate succeeds instead of raising `REFUSE to remove the
      repository root`.
- [ ] `phase_abort` run from inside a worktree restores the **main** checkout
      (`git checkout <parent-branch>` / pull), not the worktree.
- [ ] A regression test in `skill/implement/tests/` reproduces the
      resume-from-worktree start against a real temporary git repo and linked
      worktree (no `_get_repo_root` mocking), and **fails on the pre-fix code**
      while passing after the fix; a second assertion covers the stale-state
      finish path.
- [ ] `_remove_worktree`'s safety gates are unchanged in behaviour: removing
      the true main checkout is still refused (existing coverage retained), and
      the fix supplies the correct root rather than relaxing the check.
- [ ] All existing `skill/implement/tests/` tests pass via the project test
      skill, and the full project test suite passes with the new changes.
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including
      code comments, `skill/implement/SKILL.md` / `docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md`
      where they describe `repo_root`, and any relevant wiki or docs site
      entries (state file schema note: `repo_root` is always the main checkout).

## Constraints

- The fix lives in `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` in the **SorraAgents**
  framework repo (the global install is a symlink), while this work item lives
  in the MainStreet worklog. Implementation therefore runs from the SorraAgents
  checkout with the `MS-…` id; `wl` resolves the MainStreet store by
  prefix-to-sibling scan, and the commit lands on SorraAgents `dev`. Do **not**
  copy `implement.py` into this repo.
- No behavioural change beyond repo-root resolution: commit → push → worktree
  removal ordering, the test/refactor gates and the state-file schema stay as
  they are (only the value written changes).
- No hand editing of live `.implement_state.json` files and no deletion of
  existing stranded worktrees as part of this item.
- The worktree-removal safety gate must keep refusing the real main checkout —
  do not weaken it to make the symptom disappear.
- Keep the change small and local: no refactor of `_get_repo_root`, no new
  abstraction over phase plumbing.

## Key Files

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — the four call sites, named
  durably (line numbers drift; prefer the anchors): `phase_start` Step 8
  `repo_root = str(Path.cwd().resolve())` (the defect), `phase_finish`
  Step 5 `repo_root = state.repo_root if state else ...`, the
